subject: Post-call: performance parameters and streaming constraints
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <ops@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance parameters and streaming constraints

Maya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end and a few clarifying asks so we can scope a targeted performance probe. I captured the items we discussed and suggested next steps below.

Recap / requirements we heard
- Target end-to-end (client -> Orchid infra -> Redwood hosted API -> client) SLOs: p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 450 ms for single-turn responses (median token length ~60).
- Streaming paths (SSE): must support chunked streaming for responses > 512 tokens with per-chunk latency <= 60 ms and overall completion p99 <= 1.2s for long outputs.
- Concurrency envelope: sustained 120 concurrent requests (avg per-instance), burst to 600 req/s for 2–5 minutes during peak batch runs.
- Typical payload distribution attached (orchid_latency_traffic_profile.csv) — 70% short prompts (<200 tokens), 25% medium (200–600), 5% long (600–2k).
- Incumbent reported numbers on your call: p95 ~320 ms, p99 ~900 ms. Goal is clear headroom with hosted performance.

Clarifying asks (what we need from you to scope the probe)
1) Confirm whether the p99 target must include upstream DB query time and Orchid-side pre/post-processing. If yes, please share representative DB RTTs (avg and 95th).
2) For streaming, do you require ordered chunk boundaries aligned to application-level sentences, or is best-effort chunking acceptable?
3) Any TLS termination/MTU constraints on your side (we noticed some customers have 900 MTU limits that change chunking behavior).
4) Can you provision a short test token set we can run (1000 requests) against a shadow endpoint, or should we replay traffic from the CSV you attached?

Proposed next steps
- Sergio / Redwood: prepare a focused test harness (we will instrument e2e tracing and token-level timing). Deliverable: test script + dashboard. ETA: 48 hours after test data arrives.
- Orchid: share DB RTTs + confirm streaming boundary requirement. Also please send a point person for networking (Ken?).
- Schedule a 90-min probe window (we suggest Wed 19 Aug 09:00 PT).

Attachments: orchid_latency_traffic_profile.csv (sample distribution), redwood_streaming-checklist.pdf (how we measure chunk latency).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a formal test plan once we get the small bits above.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Maya Singh <ops@orchidhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance parameters and streaming constraints

Thanks Sergio — useful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) p99 requirement: must be measured end-to-end from the mobile client perspective (that includes our pre-processing time, which is usually ~30–80 ms depending on lookup). We can export a small histogram of DB RTTs — I’ll attach it if useful.
2) Streaming boundary: we prefer application-level sentence boundaries for chunk flushes to simplify replay on the mobile SDK; best-effort is acceptable for the first pass but final acceptance should preserve sentence boundaries where possible.
3) Networking: Ken (cc’d) is our infra lead — we have typical AWS MTU and TLS termination at the ALB. No special MTU constraints but there is a 2-second idle timeout on our proxy.
4) Test data: we can either give you a replayable log (preferred) or let you hit a shadow endpoint. We’ll aim to share the replay file by EOD tomorrow.

One ask from my engineering lead: please show comparison curves (p95/p99) for both the Redwood hosted path and a comparable quantized variant (if available) so we understand the tradeoffs.

Maya
Ops, Orchid Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <ops@orchidhealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance parameters and streaming constraints

Maya — quick note: we can run the shadow replay or use your log replay. I’ll book the probe window for Wed 19 Aug 09:00 PT unless you prefer otherwise. Aditya: can you confirm infra will provide warm pools and KV cache priming during the window?

Also: can you confirm what error budget looks acceptable to Orchid for the trial (p99 breach tolerance)? We typically ask for <0.5% p99 breach for a short probe to call the run representative.

— Lauren
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <ops@orchidhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ken Jacobs <ken.jacobs@orchidhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2026 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call: performance parameters and streaming constraints — agreed next steps

Thanks everyone — summarizing decisions / owners so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Agreed items
- Measurement scope: end-to-end from client (includes Orchid pre/post-processing). (Owner: Orchid — Maya/Ken)
- Probe window: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:00 UTC (09:00 PT). (Owner: Lauren to schedule calendar invite)
- Test data: Orchid will provide replayable log by EOD Tue 18 Aug. Redwood will validate format and return a runnable harness. (Owners: Orchid / Sergio)
- Warm pools & KV cache: Aditya to confirm warm instance priming and a cache-priming script; aim: steady-state during probe. (Owner: Aditya)
- Acceptance thresholds for probe (short window): p95 <= 260 ms, p99 <= 500 ms, p99 breach tolerance <= 0.5% (proposed). Note: we relaxed p95/p99 slightly from the initial ask to account for network variance; final SLA subject to sizing exercise. (Owner: Sergio / Lauren)
- Deliverables after probe: time-series p50/p95/p99 charts, token-level timing waterfall, streaming chunk latency distribution, and a short runbook describing fallback policies if thresholds are missed. (Owner: Redwood — Sergio + infra)

Open asks for Orchid before we kick off
- DB RTT histogram (avg/95th) and confirmation on proxy idle timeout behavior.
- Confirmation whether sentence-aligned streaming is a hard requirement for acceptance.

I’ll send calendar invites and upload the proposed harness to the Drive link (above) once I get the replay file. If anything here is off, flag it and I’ll update.

— Sergio
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
